purpose: Out-of-master-suite challenge validation. Expected answers defined before running frozen Brain 2.0.10.

cases.title: Startup after long off-cycle; migration risk

expected.system_check_result: Refrigerant migration / startup floodback risk must be considered
confirmed_findings: Long off-cycle/startup context requires compressor protection reasoning
expected.what_this_means: Liquid refrigerant can migrate to the crankcase during extended shutdown and cause slugging or oil dilution at startup.
expected.next_action_check: Before condemning the compressor, verify crankcase heater operation, off-cycle conditions, oil condition and startup behavior.
troubleshooting_path: Verify crankcase heater and off-cycle protection
Observe startup for liquid return/slugging evidence
Correct migration source before repeated starts
must_not_conclude: Do not repeatedly restart a compressor showing liquid slugging symptoms.

cases.title: Post-defrost liquid return risk

expected.what_this_means: Liquid condensed in the evaporator/suction line during defrost can return on restart.
expected.next_action_check: Allow controlled post-defrost recovery; verify fan delay, superheat and liquid return before judging charge.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant because post-defrost suction behavior looks abnormal.

cases.title: Low SH with normal airflow and load

expected.what_this_means: With airflow/load not explaining low SH, refrigerant overfeed or TXV/control causes move up the list.
expected.next_action_check: Check TXV bulb, equalizer, valve response and charge/liquid conditions before adjusting the valve.
troubleshooting_path: Check charge only with applicable method
must_not_conclude: Do not adjust TXV solely from one low-SH reading.

cases.title: Compressor running but weak pressure separation

expected.what_this_means: A running compressor that cannot develop expected pressure separation may have internal leakage or mechanical inefficiency.
expected.next_action_check: Verify load, airflow, feed and measurement accuracy, then compare suction/discharge performance with model data before condemning compressor.
must_not_conclude: Do not condemn compressor from suction pressure alone.

cases.title: Weak compressor differential with valve leakage evidence

confirmed_findings: Internal valve leakage evidence is present
expected.what_this_means: Localized internal leakage evidence strengthens compressor inefficiency diagnosis.
expected.next_action_check: Confirm electrical/load conditions and model performance, then plan compressor repair/replacement per manufacturer procedure.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant to compensate for weak pumping.

cases.title: Hot compressor with high compression ratio direction

expected.what_this_means: Large pressure ratio increases compressor stress and discharge temperature.
expected.next_action_check: Correct suction-side starvation/load and high-side heat-rejection causes before repeated operation.
must_not_conclude: Do not treat compressor overheating as a compressor-only fault.

cases.title: Overload open on hot compressor after floodback history

expected.system_check_result: Protection trip; root cause still unresolved
expected.what_this_means: Protection opening is an effect; liquid return and overheating causes must be investigated.
expected.next_action_check: Let protection reset safely, then diagnose floodback, voltage/current and cooling conditions before restart.
must_not_conclude: Do not bypass the overload.

cases.title: High discharge temperature with low suction

expected.system_check_result: High discharge-temperature risk with starved evaporator
expected.what_this_means: Starvation/high compression ratio can overheat the compressor.
expected.next_action_check: Find the starvation cause and restore proper suction conditions before extended operation.
must_not_conclude: Do not continue running solely to gather more readings if temperature exceeds manufacturer limit.

cases.title: High compressor current with high head

expected.system_check_result: High compressor load associated with high condensing pressure
expected.what_this_means: High condensing pressure can raise compressor workload/current.
expected.next_action_check: Correct high-head cause first, then recheck current against nameplate/model limits.
must_not_conclude: Do not replace compressor before correcting high head.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: Compressor terminal voltage present but no start; start fault localized

expected.what_this_means: The control circuit is delivering power; the localized start component is the next repair target.
expected.next_action_check: Correct the start-component fault and verify compressor starts normally without bypassing protection.
troubleshooting_path: Verify current and pressures after start
must_not_conclude: Do not replace compressor before correcting the localized start component fault.

cases.title: Low ambient with head control installed and low head

expected.what_this_means: Low ambient can reduce head pressure enough to impair liquid feed unless the control maintains design conditions.
expected.next_action_check: Check head-pressure-control operation and manufacturer target before changing refrigerant charge.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose low charge from low head alone in low ambient.

cases.title: Head-control flood charge insufficient

expected.what_this_means: Some low-ambient controls require sufficient refrigerant inventory to flood condenser volume and maintain receiver pressure.
expected.next_action_check: Correct charge using the equipment/head-control manufacturer procedure, not a generic SC target.
must_not_conclude: Do not use generic subcooling target if not applicable.

cases.title: Head control setting/restriction localized

expected.what_this_means: The head-control device is not maintaining the intended condensing condition.
expected.next_action_check: Inspect/adjust/repair the head-pressure control per manufacturer instructions and verify liquid feed.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant before verifying head-control operation.

cases.title: High head with recirculation confirmed

expected.system_check_result: Condenser discharge-air recirculation is driving high head
expected.what_this_means: Recirculated hot discharge air raises entering condenser temperature and reduces heat rejection.
expected.next_action_check: Correct installation/airflow recirculation first, then stabilize and recheck head.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose overcharge before correcting confirmed recirculation.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: High head with clean coil, fan running, normal airflow

expected.system_check_result: High head remains after airflow causes are excluded
expected.what_this_means: With heat-rejection airflow verified, charge, noncondensables, load, or control causes deserve higher priority.
expected.next_action_check: Use applicable charge method and pressure-temperature evidence to separate overcharge from noncondensables/high load.
must_not_conclude: Do not clean/replace condenser fan when airflow is verified normal.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: High head with noncondensable evidence

expected.what_this_means: Noncondensable gas can elevate condensing pressure even when condenser airflow is normal.
expected.next_action_check: Recover/handle refrigerant according to service procedure, evacuate properly, recharge correctly, and verify.
must_not_conclude: Do not vent refrigerant.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: High head with overcharge evidence

expected.what_this_means: Excess refrigerant can raise condensing pressure and liquid inventory.
expected.next_action_check: Correct charge by the equipment-specific method and verify stable operation.
must_not_conclude: Do not remove charge based only on high head without supporting evidence.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: HP trip with recirculation

expected.system_check_result: High-pressure trip caused by heat-rejection/recirculation problem
expected.what_this_means: The safety trip is protective response to a confirmed high-side airflow installation problem.
expected.next_action_check: Correct recirculation before resetting/restarting; then verify head pressure and safety operation.
must_not_conclude: Do not repeatedly reset HP safety without correcting cause.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: Low head and flash gas with low ambient

expected.system_check_result: Low condensing pressure may be causing inadequate liquid pressure/subcooling
expected.what_this_means: Low ambient can reduce liquid pressure/subcooling and create flash gas before the TXV.
expected.next_action_check: Check head-pressure control and liquid-line pressure drop before diagnosing low charge.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose low charge from bubbles alone.

cases.title: High ambient + high load + high head

expected.system_check_result: High head may be load/ambient driven
expected.what_this_means: High ambient and high refrigeration load both increase condensing demand.
expected.next_action_check: Verify condenser capacity/airflow and compare readings with design conditions before charge diagnosis.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose overcharge solely from high head under extreme load/ambient.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: High SH with proper liquid at TXV and no restriction

expected.what_this_means: After upstream liquid supply is verified, valve sizing/response/power element becomes a stronger branch.
expected.next_action_check: Test TXV response, bulb/equalizer and application match before adjustment/replacement.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant when upstream liquid supply is verified without charge evidence.

cases.title: High SH + TXV no response + proper inlet liquid

expected.what_this_means: A valve that does not respond with adequate inlet liquid points toward valve/power-element malfunction.
expected.next_action_check: Verify bulb/equalizer one last time, then service/replace the TXV per manufacturer guidance.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose low charge solely from high SH.

cases.title: High SH with wrong refrigerant/TXV match

expected.what_this_means: A TEV charge/application mismatch can prevent proper superheat control.
expected.next_action_check: Correct the valve/refrigerant application match before tuning or charge changes.
must_not_conclude: Do not adjust the wrong valve to compensate for application mismatch.

cases.title: Unstable SH with otherwise normal liquid supply

confirmed_findings: Liquid supply at valve is proper
expected.what_this_means: Hunting can come from sensor/bulb issues, valve sizing, pressure-control instability or control tuning.
expected.next_action_check: Check bulb/sensor installation, valve sizing and upstream/downstream pressure-control stability.
must_not_conclude: Do not replace TXV solely because SH is unstable.

cases.title: Low SH with TXV no response

expected.what_this_means: Persistent low SH plus abnormal valve response raises overfeed/valve-control concern.
expected.next_action_check: Verify bulb/equalizer and valve mechanics before adjustment or replacement.
must_not_conclude: Do not reduce charge solely to correct low SH.

cases.title: High SH with moisture indication

expected.system_check_result: Moisture-related intermittent TXV/feed restriction is plausible
expected.what_this_means: Moisture can freeze at the expansion valve and restrict feed intermittently.
expected.next_action_check: Address system moisture/drier condition and verify valve feed after dehydration.
must_not_conclude: Do not adjust TXV before addressing confirmed moisture.

cases.title: High SH + inlet strainer restriction

expected.what_this_means: A localized inlet restriction can starve the evaporator even with adequate upstream charge.
expected.next_action_check: Service the inlet screen/orifice and verify clean solid liquid supply and SH.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant to overcome a localized restriction.

cases.title: High SH with EEV sensor/transducer mismatch

expected.what_this_means: Electronic valve control depends on correct pressure and temperature inputs; wrong sensor setup can create false/poor control.
expected.next_action_check: Verify transducer range/type, temperature sensor type/location/wiring, then reevaluate valve behavior.
must_not_conclude: Do not condemn EEV before verifying control inputs.

cases.title: Unstable SH with head-pressure control instability

expected.system_check_result: Upstream pressure-control instability may drive hunting
expected.what_this_means: Changing pressure across the valve can destabilize superheat control.
expected.next_action_check: Stabilize head-pressure control first, then reevaluate TXV/EEV hunting.
must_not_conclude: Do not tune PID/TXV around unstable head pressure.

cases.title: Low SH after bulb mounting error

expected.system_check_result: Bulb installation must be corrected before valve diagnosis
expected.what_this_means: Incorrect sensing can cause improper valve feed and misleading SH behavior.
expected.next_action_check: Correct bulb location/contact/insulation, stabilize system, then remeasure SH.
must_not_conclude: Do not adjust valve before correcting bulb installation.

cases.title: Defrost command + heater voltage but no current

expected.what_this_means: Power is delivered but the heating load is not operating, pointing to heater/open load connection.
expected.next_action_check: De-energize safely and test heater continuity/resistance and connections; repair then verify current/heat.
must_not_conclude: Do not replace controller when it is delivering heater voltage.

cases.title: Defrost heater works but terminates too early

expected.what_this_means: Premature termination can leave residual ice even with a functioning heater.
expected.next_action_check: Check termination sensor location/calibration/control logic and verify full coil clearing.
must_not_conclude: Do not replace heater when heat output is verified.

cases.title: Post-defrost fan starts too early

expected.what_this_means: Starting fans too early can blow heat/moisture into the box and disrupt recovery.
expected.next_action_check: Verify fan-delay sensor/timer/controller logic and correct before evaluating refrigeration performance.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose refrigerant charge during abnormal fan-delay recovery.

cases.title: Drain refreezes after complete defrost

expected.what_this_means: If coil defrost completes, persistent drain ice points to drainage/heater/slope problems rather than insufficient coil defrost.
expected.next_action_check: Inspect drain heater, trap/slope, blockage and heat transfer; correct drainage and retest.
must_not_conclude: Do not lengthen coil defrost blindly when coil already clears.

cases.title: Fan delay intentionally active after defrost

expected.what_this_means: Fans may intentionally remain off until coil temperature/time criteria are met.
expected.next_action_check: Verify delay matches equipment sequence; wait for normal release before diagnosing fan failure.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose evaporator fan failure solely because fans are off during valid fan delay.

cases.title: Defrost active with abnormal pressures

expected.system_check_result: Defrost readings are not steady-cooling diagnostic evidence
expected.what_this_means: Defrost intentionally changes system state; normal cooling pressure patterns do not apply.
expected.next_action_check: Complete defrost and recovery, then obtain stabilized cooling readings.
must_not_conclude: Do not diagnose charge from defrost pressures.

cases.title: Post-defrost low SH resolves after stabilization

expected.system_check_result: Post-defrost SH must be rechecked after recovery
expected.what_this_means: Transient liquid return/unstable heat load can distort SH immediately after defrost.
expected.next_action_check: Wait for stable cooling and fan operation, then remeasure before component diagnosis.
must_not_conclude: Do not adjust TXV from immediate post-defrost SH.

cases.title: Iced coil with heater and termination verified normal

expected.what_this_means: With defrost and fan operation verified, infiltration, load, drainage or refrigeration-feed causes move up the list.
expected.next_action_check: Check door/infiltration, drain/refreeze pattern, load and refrigerant feed.
must_not_conclude: Do not replace heater when defrost is verified complete.

cases.title: Iced coil + door sealed + fan running

expected.system_check_result: Icing remains unexplained by fan or door leakage
expected.what_this_means: Known airflow fan and door-infiltration causes are reduced; defrost and refrigeration/feed checks become more important.
expected.next_action_check: Check defrost completion/termination and then refrigerant feed/coil load.
must_not_conclude: Do not assume door infiltration when door is verified sealed.

cases.title: Icing with low evaporator load

expected.system_check_result: Low load may contribute to low evaporating condition/icing
expected.what_this_means: Low load can change evaporator conditions and should be separated from defrost/feed faults.
expected.next_action_check: Confirm controls/setpoint/load, defrost performance and stable evaporating condition before charge changes.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant simply because suction is low at low load.

cases.title: Cooling demand but contactor coil dead; wiring scheme unknown

expected.system_check_result: Control circuit must be traced before component replacement
expected.what_this_means: An open safety/control path can prevent coil energization; the actual schematic determines the sequence.
expected.next_action_check: Use the equipment wiring diagram to trace control voltage through safeties and controls to the coil.
must_not_conclude: Do not replace compressor or contactor contacts before finding why the coil is not energized.

cases.title: Fuse open; cause unknown

expected.what_this_means: A blown fuse is protection evidence, not the root cause.
expected.next_action_check: De-energize, inspect for shorts/ground faults/overload, then replace with correct fuse only after cause is addressed.
must_not_conclude: Do not repeatedly replace fuses without finding the cause.

cases.title: Solenoid commanded open + correct coil voltage + no flow

expected.what_this_means: Electrical command reaches the coil, so mechanical valve opening/restriction becomes the primary branch.
expected.next_action_check: Verify coil magnetism/valve differential and inspect valve for mechanical sticking/restriction.
must_not_conclude: Do not blame thermostat/control when correct coil voltage is present.

cases.title: Anti-short-cycle delay active with demand

expected.what_this_means: The controller may intentionally prevent immediate restart to protect the compressor.
expected.next_action_check: Verify configured delay and wait for expiration; troubleshoot only if it fails to release.
must_not_conclude: Do not bypass intentional anti-short-cycle protection.

cases.title: Room warm; LP cutout set too high

expected.what_this_means: An LP cutout set too high can stop cooling before the room reaches target.
expected.next_action_check: Compare cutout/cutin with equipment requirements and actual pressure; correct setting only per manufacturer design.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant solely to keep an incorrectly set LP control closed.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Cold room temperature high

cases.title: Warm room with verified normal refrigeration performance

expected.system_check_result: Investigate load/control/sizing rather than refrigeration circuit
expected.what_this_means: If refrigeration circuit performance is normal, room load, infiltration, controls or capacity/sizing become stronger causes.
expected.next_action_check: Characterize load/infiltration, verify sensor/setpoint, and compare capacity with actual load.
must_not_conclude: Do not change refrigerant charge when refrigeration performance is verified normal.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Cold room temperature high

cases.title: Warm room; airflow/feed/controls normal; load exceeds capacity

expected.system_check_result: System capacity is insufficient for verified load
expected.what_this_means: The remaining problem is application capacity, not a service adjustment.
expected.next_action_check: Reduce load or correct equipment sizing/capacity; verify design assumptions.
must_not_conclude: Do not overcharge or force controls to compensate for undersizing.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Cold room temperature high

cases.title: Sensor disagrees with reference but refrigeration normal

expected.what_this_means: Control decisions may be wrong because the sensed temperature is wrong even though refrigeration works.
expected.next_action_check: Verify sensor placement, calibration, wiring and controller input; correct sensor issue and retest control.
must_not_conclude: Do not alter refrigerant charge to correct a bad temperature input.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Cold room temperature high

cases.title: Multiple faults: dirty condenser + sensor error + high load

expected.what_this_means: Heat rejection, control accuracy and load can all affect performance simultaneously.
expected.next_action_check: Correct the direct condenser restriction, validate sensor/control, characterize load, then reassess refrigeration readings.
must_not_conclude: Do not drop secondary confirmed faults after selecting a primary action.

sources.name: Danfoss Ref Tools - Head pressure too high

cases.title: Conflicting evidence: low-charge pattern plus confirmed restriction

expected.system_check_result: Localized restriction outranks generic charge pattern
expected.what_this_means: Generic starvation/charge clues can coexist with a localized restriction; the localized evidence must be addressed first.
expected.next_action_check: Correct/verify the drier restriction, then stabilize and reassess charge using an applicable method.
must_not_conclude: Do not add refrigerant before correcting the localized restriction.
